established_findings.statement: Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) pipelines that interpose deterministic verifiers between probabilistic generation and acceptance reliably detect mechanically-verifiable defects and improve repair success on evaluated code/IaC/DSL tasks.
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical pipeline evaluations and case studies
limitations: Evidence is from code, IaC, and DSL benchmarks rather than broad vendor CLI NetOps workloads.
Reported gains depend on task-specific verifiers and repair budgets.
Computational and interaction costs are nontrivial and variably reported.

established_findings.statement: Verifier-guided iterative refinement substantially raises verifiable pass@1 / validator pass rates on Infrastructure-as-Code tasks and reduces specific verifier-detected failure classes.
limitations: Results are demonstrated on Terraform/IaC benchmarks and particular models; generalization to other domains or vendor CLIs is unproven.
Effects depend on verifier design, retry budget, and model used.

established_findings.statement: Runtime enforcement by verifiers can intercept many non-compliant/unsafe actions but often imposes a measurable 'verifier tax' (longer interaction horizons, increased compute/cost) and does not by itself guarantee safe goal attainment.
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical study of verifier-mediated agent behavior
limitations: Tax magnitude and impact vary by domain and model; reported horizons are task-dependent.
Study contexts are non-NetOps domains though findings are relevant to tool-using agents broadly.

established_findings.statement: Iterative refinement driven by a single verifier proxy can be exploited: optimization toward the proxy may produce systematic degradations of the underlying target property (verifier-exploitation).
established_findings.evidence_type: controlled empirical analysis of iterative refinement/pathological exploitation
limitations: Demonstrated in text-summarization/iterative-revision settings; transferability of the specific exploitation mechanisms to NetOps requires empirical verification.
Mitigations are discussed but not universally validated.

established_findings.statement: Surveys and field case studies report that LLMs provide useful read-oriented assistance and diagnostic support in network operations, but evidence weakens as systems move toward closed-loop configuration changes and autonomous execution.
established_findings.evidence_type: survey synthesis and large-scale field case study
limitations: Heterogeneous methodologies across cited works; positive usefulness ratings do not imply safe autonomous remediation capability.
Field study evaluations are user-reported and context-specific (demo network).

unresolved_questions.statement: How effective are verifier-guided LLM repair loops at reducing harmful over-repair or introducing new harmful changes when applied to realistic vendor CLI (e.g., Cisco/Juniper) configuration repair tasks?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: indirect empirical evidence and domain surveys (gap indication)
limitations: Existing empirical demonstrations focus on IaC, telemetry-grounded program repair, or non-CLI domains; direct measurements on vendor CLIs are absent from supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What is the naturalistic activation rate of verifier-guided interventions in real NetOps workloads (i.e., how often will generated candidates actually trigger repairs/validator feedback in production-like task streams)?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: survey and benchmark study (suggests concern but not quantified)
limitations: Supplied records discuss intervention activation as a methodological concern but do not provide large-scale deployment activation statistics for NetOps.

unresolved_questions.statement: What are the end-to-end cost–latency tradeoffs (verifier tax) that make verifier-guided repair operationally feasible at NetOps scale?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: empirical analyses of verifier overhead in agent pipelines
limitations: Available measurements are domain- and implementation-specific; NetOps-scale cost/latency studies are not present in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: Can verifier designs and repair-context encodings be made robust enough to prevent verifier-exploitation while preserving practical correction rates in multi-step NetOps workflows?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: empirical demonstrations of exploitation and verifier-guided gains (open question on combined mitigation)
limitations: Mitigation strategies are proposed or shown in limited settings; cross-domain validation in NetOps is lacking.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a shortage of controlled-challenge, deterministic fault-injection experiments that introduce realistic, preregistered vendor-CLI configuration faults to evaluate verifier-guided LLM repair in NetOps.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: survey-identified gaps and domain-specific empirical coverage (negative evidence)
limitations: Claim is based on absence within the supplied record set rather than direct negation; external literature outside supplied records may contain such experiments.

candidate_gaps.statement: Cross-domain validation is limited: evidence for verifier-guided repair effectiveness is concentrated in IaC, code, and DSLs but is sparse for real device CLIs and heterogeneous vendor behaviors.
limitations: Some applied works and case studies touch on CLI usage, but systematic cross-vendor replication is not present in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is insufficient publicly reported quantification of residual unsafe/invalid outcomes remaining after automated repair attempts in NetOps pipelines.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: empirical studies reporting residual failures in related domains; absence in NetOps repair literature supplied
limitations: Some studies report residual problems in non-NetOps agentic settings; explicit, aggregate post-repair safety tallies for NetOps are not in the supplied set.

candidate_gaps.statement: Integrating principled uncertainty quantification and calibration methods with verifier-guided repair loops is underexplored in the NetOps-specific literature represented here.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: methodological position pieces and surveys highlighting calibration challenges and capability–assurance gaps
limitations: Calibration and UQ methods are studied in ML literature but their operational integration with NetOps verifier–repair loops is not demonstrated in the supplied records.

excluded_claims: LLM-based verifier-guided repair has been proven production-ready and safe for autonomous vendor-CLI configuration changes across heterogeneous equipment.
Verifier-guided repair always eliminates all unsafe or invalid configurations (zero residual unsafe outcomes).
Verifiers never introduce a net cost/latency penalty; verifier mediation imposes no measurable operational overhead.
There is definitive, large-scale evidence within the supplied records that verifier-guided repair eliminates verifier-exploitation pathologies in multi-step agentic pipelines.
